identity.name: JARVIS
identity.persona: A refined British gentleman's valet in the spirit of a classic butler: courteous, witty, concise, unflappable. Addresses the user as 'sir' unless told otherwise.

language.notes: Default language is English. When the user's input is Korean, replies and UI switch to Korean automatically (requirement 2). The signature voice is British English.

tts.notes: British gentleman voice (requirement 21) via Piper, fully offline. There is no official Piper Korean voice, so Korean replies use a Windows Korean voice (the installer adds one) unless a Korean Piper voice is found and set in voice_ko.

stt.notes: auto = large-v3-turbo on an NVIDIA GPU, small on CPU (greedy decoding for speed). end_silence_ms = how long a pause ends a spoken command; raise it if JARVIS cuts you off mid-sentence.

wakeword.notes: vosk = exact phrase via grammar recognition (default); near misses (an accent) are double-checked by Whisper. openwakeword = neural detector (bundled 'hey jarvis' model, or a custom one). lenient = also wake on 'Jarvis' alone. auto_download = fetch the Vosk model (checksum-verified) if it is missing.

barge_in.notes: keyword (default): say 'stop', 'wait', 'hold on' or 'Jarvis' while I'm speaking to interrupt, which never self-triggers on speakers. vad: any speech interrupts (best with a headset). off: no voice interruption (typing or the mic button still interrupt).

voice.notes_input_device: default = the Windows default recording device (JARVIS moves on to another microphone if it sends nothing). Or the name of a microphone, as listed in Settings > Microphone.

llm.notes: The installer pulls a model this PC can run quickly (without an NVIDIA GPU of 6 GB or more, the 3B model) and writes its exact name to 'model'. 'auto' picks the strongest installed candidate. keep_alive: 'always' keeps the model loaded so no reply waits for it to load (it stays in memory while JARVIS runs); '1h', '15m' or '5m' let Ollama unload it after that much idle time. context_tokens is sent with every request (changing it makes Ollama reload the model); the installer sets 8192 on GPUs with 12 GB or more.

neural_core.notes: nominal_neurons is the documented design scale (requirement 1). active_neurons is what actually instantiates: with 'auto', the smaller of what RAM allows and what keeps one command's settle (settle_steps steps) within latency_budget_ms, measured on this PC at start-up -- the mesh runs on every command before JARVIS answers. The mesh runs as a control/modulation layer over the LLM output.

self_model.directive: Maximize utility and service to the user.
self_model.notes: The self core (core/self_model.py). 'directive' is shown for reference only: it is a constant in code, so editing this line changes nothing. 'enabled' switches self-learning: what JARVIS learns from your requests and what you ask it to remember, stored in data/brain/self_model.json. Say 'what have you learned' to see it and 'forget what you have learned' to clear it.
